name: IRLNEP Habitat Restoration Projects RFP

funder.name: Indian River Lagoon Council (Indian River Lagoon National Estuary Program)

summary: Local funding for on-the-ground habitat restoration in Florida's Indian River Lagoon, such as seagrass, oyster and other filter-feeder restoration, living shorelines, and design and engineering of restoration sites. Nonprofits can apply on their own.
reporting: Funded projects submit quarterly progress reports from the first quarter after contract execution until the project is complete.

steps: Proposal package by email, as a PDF
Completeness check by IRL Council staff
Scoring by the proposal review committee
Management Conference review and Council Board decision

eligibility.rule: Applicant is not an individual property owner or property association
Project outputs and outcomes align with the IRLNEP Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan
Funding is not to bring an organisation into compliance with a permit
Private land: public agency or nonprofit lead, owner partner with direct or in-kind support, and public benefit
Design and engineering projects are completed within 12 months
Not a habitat assessment or inventory on its own
Not a project focused on citizen engagement
Document quantified restoration metrics, such as acres or linear feet restored

documents: Project location map and at least one representative photo, attached separately as JPEG/PNG at 300 dpi or higher
Cover letter from the director or another person authorised to submit
Letter from each funding partner endorsing the project and stating its role and commitment
Signed Scrutinized Companies certification (Exhibit A), for-profit companies only
Private land: owner’s support letter with proof of ownership and access, liability and applicable land-use assurances
Copy of a federal NICRA, if indirect costs exceed 15%
Detailed project budget with cost and match breakdown
Letters of support for cash or in-kind match providers not covered by partner letters

status.quote: Category 2: Habitat Restoration Projects Open from October 15, 2026

opens.quote: Proposal packages will be accepted beginning on October 15, 2026, and are due by Monday December 14, 2026, by 5:00 p.m.

deadline.quote: Proposal packages will be accepted beginning on October 15, 2026, and are due by Monday December 14, 2026, by 5:00 p.m.

applicant_types.quote: The Applicant must be a public agency or not-for profit organization

geography.quote: IRL Council funds may be used for projects within the formal IRLNEP watershed boundary (Ponce de Leon Inlet, Volusia County to Jupiter Inlet, Palm Beach County)

access.quote: Proposal packages will be accepted beginning on October 15, 2026, and are due by Monday December 14, 2026, by 5:00 p.m.

window.quote: Proposal packages will be accepted beginning on October 15, 2026, and are due by Monday December 14, 2026, by 5:00 p.m.

amount.quote: Applicants can request a minimum of $25,000 up to $100,000.

pool.quote: In FY 2028 approximately $100,000 is expected to be available for habitat restoration projects.

co_finance_required.quote: Habitat restoration projects must demonstrate a minimum cost-share match of 50% of the total project cost of the project being proposed.

reporting.quote: The recipient shall submit quarterly progress reports starting after the first quarter following contract execution and continuing to project completion.

effort.quote: Applications for project funding are due no later than 5:00 p.m., December 14, 2026.
Proposals will be reviewed by the IRL Council staff to determine if the proposal is complete (responsive) pursuant to RFP instructions herein.
All responsive proposals will be reviewed and scored independently and individually by members of the proposal review committee.

The IRL Council Board of Directors make the final decision on project funding pursuant to proposal review, ranking, and recommendations from proposal review committees drawn from the IRLNEP Management Conference and availability of funds.
Proposals are required to be submitted via electronic mail in Portable Document Format (PDF) only

eligibility.quote: Individual property owners or property associations are not eligible as primary proposal applicants.
Habitat restoration project outputs and outcomes MUST align with the IRLNEP Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan (CCMP) – Looking Ahead to 2030.
Any project that is requesting funding to bring an organization into compliance with a permit is not eligible

1. The Applicant must be a public agency or not-for profit organization; 2. The private property owner (individual or association) must be a partner on the project with direct and/or inkind support; 3. The project must be in the public good
D&E projects MUST be completed within a 12- month period.
Habitat assessments or inventories. These may be accomplished as a task or deliverable along with restoration activities but will not be considered habitat restoration.
Projects focused on citizen engagement will not be considered under this RFP.
Project proposals must document quantified restoration metrics such as acres to be restored, linear feet restored, number of filter feeders added, etc.

co_finance.quote: Quantify and show calculations for all in-kind match. Note that Indirect Costs (Facilities and Administrative, F&A) will NOT be accepted as cost share. Habitat Restoration Projects (Category 2) are required to have a Minimum 50% (dollar for dollar) match of the Total Project costs.

consortium_required.quote: No, as a non-profit you may apply without a partner, however, project reviewers often find partner collaboration enhances projects.

after_award.quote: The recipient shall submit quarterly progress reports starting after the first quarter following contract execution and continuing to project completion.

documents.quote: The proposal must be accompanied by a cover letter from the director, or another person authorized to submit the proposal for the organization or company.
The proposal must be accompanied by a letter from an authorized representative of each funding partner listed in the proposal.
A signed scrutinized companies form, Exhibit A, (Only for a company as defined in section 215.473 F.S.; i.e. “for profit”).
A copy of a Federal NICRA is required if requesting over 15%.

Provide as a separate attachment a map of the project location and at least one high-resolution photo representative of the project (site plan, technology, work of volunteers, etc.). These should be in JPEG or PNG format and a minimum of 300 dpi. Do NOT embed these images in a document.

Written support letter from the property owner of record with documentation of ownership and statement that owner is willing to accept the following: access to property for Applicant to implement the work, liability waiver, in-perpetuity conservation easement or restrictive covenant on land to be improved (if applicable) and long-term maintenance and management plan (if applicable).
The one-page executive summary is in the format defined per the instructions herein and included with the proposal.
Include a description of all costs and detailed accounting of in-kind and cash match, and sources of all funds.
All providers of matching funds (cash or in-kind) must be quantified in the budget and supported by organization letters of support.
